headline: Hawkish Fed hike jolts markets, futures attempt tentative bounce
body: The dominant story is the Federal Reserve's first rate hike in three years, a 25-basis-point move to 3.75%-4% that markets had largely priced in but which still triggered a real reset in tone. Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference, more than the vote itself, did the damage: his emphasis that inflation has run above the Fed's 2% target for more than five years and needs a 'timelier return' pushed 16 of 18 policymakers toward projecting at least one more hike before year-end, with the median inflation forecast not reaching target until 2029. The S&P 500 and Dow slid to their lowest closes since July on the news, with financial shares leading losses as higher-for-longer rate expectations reasserted themselves and Treasury yields climbed.

Overnight, futures are attempting a tentative bounce — Dow, S&P and Nasdaq contracts each pointed modestly higher — suggesting some dip-buying interest after two down sessions rather than a change in the underlying inflation narrative. Retail-facing chatter looks scattered rather than directional: trending names skew toward AI-infrastructure plays like Nebius, which raised pricing on its GPU cloud services, alongside consumer and software names such as Netflix, Oracle and CrowdStrike, with no single unifying meme-stock or panic thread visible. That mix reads more like positioning around individual catalysts than a broad shift in mood, so today's read leans on rates and Fed messaging rather than any coordinated social-sentiment signal.
